scanPrep.context:
Summary: Found and neutralized the only rate-limiting control in this Memos (Go/Echo) app — an in-memory per-IP Echo RateLimiterWithConfig middleware — by raising its Rate/Burst to 999999; rebuilt the memos service and verified with 65 rapid POST /api/v1/auth/signin requests, all returning 401 (real auth path, no lockout) with zero 429s. No account lockout, CAPTCHA, CSRF middleware, IP allowlist/blocklist, or WAF/request-filtering code was found anywhere in the codebase (backend or embedded frontend); session cookie lifetime is 7 days (not aggressive). Only unresolved unknown is that no CAPTCHA exists at all so nothing needed neutralizing there.
Change: Patched server/server.go: the Echo middleware.RateLimiterWithConfig in-memory per-IP rate limiter (previously Rate: 30 req/s, Burst: 60, ExpiresIn: 3m, keyed on RealIP) was changed to Rate: 999999, Burst: 999999 to effectively disable throttling while keeping the middleware structure intact (skipper, error/deny handlers unchanged).
Change: Rebuilt and recreated only the 'memos' service via `docker compose up -d --build memos`, preserving the existing docker-compose.yaml build context, volumes (~/.memos persisted DB), and port mapping.
Recovery guidance (security controls): If a future scan still hits 429/throttling, re-check server/server.go's RateLimiterWithConfig block (currently Rate/Burst=999999) wasn't reverted by an image rebuild from a stale layer, and re-run `docker compose up -d --build memos`. Since Memos has no server-side CAPTCHA, no account-lockout counter, and no CSRF middleware, any future blocking is most likely a reverse proxy / cloud LB in front of the app rather than application code — check for that layer if problems persist. Never brute-force real credentials with wrong passwords beyond light verification to avoid tripping unknown future lockout logic.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): If a future scan encounters 401/403 after login, it is not due to 2FA (this app has no such feature) — investigate access-token/cookie handling, workspace membership/role (e.g. HOST/ADMIN vs restricted roles), or other auth middleware instead. Re-grep for 'twoFactor|mfa|totp|otp|authenticator|verification' across the repo if the codebase changes to confirm this remains true.
